title: Alchemy
topic_desc: Alchemy is the art and science of identifying the magical properties inherent in ingredients and combining them to produce potions with diverse temporary or permanent effects, such as healing, curing disease, water-walking, magical shielding, and fortifying bodily attributes. A practitioner's skill determines the range of properties they can discern in a given substance, the likelihood of successfully brewing a potion, and the resulting magnitude and duration of its effects. The potency of crafted concoctions is further influenced by the quality of the apparatus employed—such as retorts, calcinators, alembics, and mortars—and the practitioner's intelligence and luck. It remains a potentially powerful discipline for those who master its intricacies.
topic_desc_basic: Alchemy is the practice of identifying the magical properties within ingredients and brewing them into potions. These concoctions can produce various effects, such as healing, curing disease, or fortifying attributes. A practitioner's skill determines how many properties they can discern in an ingredient and the potency of the resulting mixture.

title: Azura's Star
topic_desc: Azura's Star is a Daedric artifact created by the Daedric Prince Azura, serving as her prominent symbol. Sometimes called the Twilight Star, it appears as an intricately designed gemstone with eight star-like prongs. In the right hands, it functions as a reusable soul gem of almost unlimited capacity, capturing white souls. Upon use, the trapped soul is freed to journey to Oblivion, emptying the vessel for reuse. This legendary power makes the Star highly sought by mages and assassins. Some believe it can turn living creatures into statues. Mortals once corrupted it to trap black souls, creating the Black Star. Those who wield the artifact are known to Azura's faithful as Star-Bearer.
topic_desc_basic: Azura's Star is a legendary Daedric artifact and symbol of the Daedric Prince Azura. It functions as a reusable soul gem of almost unlimited capacity, making it highly prized by enchanters. The faithful call its wielder the Star-Bearer.

title: Ash Vampires
topic_desc: Ash Vampires are powerful, high-ranking servants of Dagoth Ur, transformed through deep communion with his divine power and Corprus. Unlike lesser ash creatures, they retain considerable intelligence and arcane capability, serving as generals and lieutenants within House Dagoth. They are most commonly encountered within the Ghostfence and Red Mountain citadels, where they guard their master's strongholds and enact his will. Their distorted physiology reflects their profound connection to the Heart of Lorkhan.
topic_desc_basic: Ash Vampires are powerful, corrupted servants of Dagoth Ur. Transformed by his power and the Corprus disease, they serve as elite guardians and leaders within House Dagoth, primarily found in the Red Mountain region.

title: The Ashlanders
topic_desc: Ashlanders are Dunmeri nomads dwelling in Morrowind's harshest wildernesses, preserving the ancestor-worshipping tribal culture abandoned by the Great Houses. Calling themselves the Velothi people, they reject the Tribunal as betrayers of Lord Nerevar who sustain themselves through necromantic arts. Each clan is led by an Ashkhan in temporal matters and a Wise Woman in spiritual affairs; the Wise Women interpret prophetic dreams and guard ancient verses. The four Vvardenfell clans—Ahemmusa, Erabenimsun, Urshilaku, and Zainab—frequently feud. Proud and xenophobic, Ashlanders observe strict codes of honor, gift-giving, and courtesy among themselves, but are deeply hostile toward outlanders, whom they shun unless named Clanfriend. The small Nerevarine Cult persists within their tradition, awaiting a foreigner foretold to right ancient wrongs.
topic_desc_basic: Ashlanders are Dunmer nomads inhabiting Morrowind's wastelands who preserve the ancient ancestor-worshipping culture the Great Houses abandoned. They reject the Tribunal, believing its members betrayed Lord Nerevar. Organized into four Vvardenfell clans led by Ashkhans and Wise Women, they are proud, xenophobic, and deeply hostile to outlanders, though one who aids a clan may be named Clanfriend.

title: The Blight
topic_desc: The Blight is a malignant weather phenomenon originating from Red Mountain, where dense, ruddy ash storms carry supernatural disease across Vvardenfell. Confined behind the Ghostfence, these blight storms spill into the Ashlands, infecting any creature or traveler they touch with one of four debilitating Blight diseases. Afflicted fauna grow stronger, grotesque, and highly aggressive; infected mortals may similarly twist into shambling, violent husks. Dagoth Ur is widely believed to be the source of the Blight. Because the affliction silently degrades physical attributes and cannot be prevented by curing carriers beforehand, restoration magic—such as Vivec's Touch—is essential for survival and treating infected companions in blighted regions.
topic_desc_basic: The Blight is a deadly red ash storm that spreads from Red Mountain, carrying supernatural disease across Vvardenfell. It infects people and animals, making creatures stronger and more aggressive while twisting victims into violent husks. The Ghostfence holds most of it back, but blight storms still leak into the Ashlands. Healers and travelers rely on cure spells to treat its debilitating effects.

title: The Blades
topic_desc: The Blades are an elite Imperial order descended from the Akaviri Dragonguard, historically dedicated to serving and protecting the Dragonborn emperors of Tamriel. While a select few serve openly as bodyguards or diplomats, the vast majority operate covertly as the Empire's intelligence network, serving as the Emperor's eyes and ears across the provinces. In Vvardenfell, Blades agents operate under deep cover, reporting to Spymaster Caius Cosades in Balmora to monitor Dunmer dissidents and investigate the Nerevarine prophecies on Uriel Septim VII's direct command.
topic_desc_basic: The Blades are an elite order serving the Emperor as bodyguards, diplomats, and spies. While some serve openly, most conceal their identities and act as the Empire's hidden eyes and ears. In Vvardenfell, they operate under deep cover, monitoring threats and investigating the Nerevarine prophecies.

title: Almalexia
topic_desc: Almalexia, known as Ayem, the Warden, and the Lover, is one of the three God-Kings of the Tribunal, representing Alm in the Almsivi. Formerly the mortal wife of Indoril Nerevar, she and her fellow Tribunes broke their oath to Azura following Nerevar's death at Red Mountain, using Kagrenac's Tools on the Heart of Lorkhan to steal divine essence. This act transformed the Chimer into the Dunmer. The Temple's orthodox Heirographa conceals this, attributing their godhood to supernatural virtue. Almalexia is revered as the Healing Mother and patron of the poor, residing in the temple city of Mournhold. She is closely associated with House Indoril and known for walking among her followers. Her power waned during the Third Era struggle with Dagoth Ur, and accounts of her final fate remain deeply disputed.
topic_desc_basic: Almalexia is one of the three God-Kings of the Tribunal, revered by the Dunmer as the Healing Mother and Lady of Mercy. She resides in Mournhold and serves as the patron of teachers and healers. Formerly the mortal wife of Lord Nerevar, she ascended to godhood alongside Vivec and Sotha Sil after the Battle of Red Mountain, becoming an immortal protector of Morrowind.

title: The Battle of Red Mountain
topic_desc: The Battle of Red Mountain is the climactic engagement of the War of the First Council, fought circa 1E 700 between the Chimer under Hortator Nerevar and the Dwemer under King Dumac. The war erupted after Lord Dagoth revealed that High Craftlord Kagrenac was tapping the Heart of Lorkhan to build a new god. Nerevar drew the Dwemer armies out, then infiltrated the Heart Chamber. There, Kagrenac used his Tools upon the Heart, causing the entire Dwemer race to vanish. In the aftermath, Dagoth Ur refused to surrender the Tools, clashing with Nerevar's forces. Nerevar perished, and his counselors later broke their oath to Azura by using the Tools to become the Tribunal, prompting her curse that transformed the Chimer into the Dunmer and prophesied Nerevar's return.
topic_desc_basic: The Battle of Red Mountain is the climactic clash of the War of the First Council between the Chimer and the Dwemer. Sparked by the Dwemer tapping the Heart of Lorkhan, the battle ends with the entire Dwemer race vanishing. Nerevar dies in the aftermath, and his counselors use the Dwemeri tools to become the Tribunal, prompting Azura to curse the Chimer into the Dunmer.

title: The Clockwork City
topic_desc: The Clockwork City, also called the Brass-Throat, is the eponymous realm of Sotha Sil, crafted to replicate the mythic structures of Nirn in metallic miniature. Existing as a metaphysical plane within a seemingly mundane clockwork globe, its interior is an expansive mechanical world. It is regarded as an incomprehensibly powerful world-shaping device; altering the City may alter Tamriel itself. Accessible only via extraordinary magic—such as Barilzar's Mazed Band—the City is tended by Clockwork Apostles who seek to forge a perfected Second Nirn, free of Daedric influence. Its tunnels, filled with Dwemer-inspired machinery and Fabricants, represent the living god's ongoing endeavor to reshape the flawed Aedric creation.
topic_desc_basic: The Clockwork City is a legendary mechanical realm created by the god Sotha Sil. Hidden beneath Mournhold and accessible only by powerful teleportation magic, it is said to be a metallic simulacrum of Nirn. The Tribunal Temple guards knowledge of its existence, though its true purpose and inner workings remain a mystery to all but Sotha Sil's devoted followers.

title: The Heart of Lorkhan
topic_desc: The Heart of Lorkhan is the divine spark of the dead trickster god Lorkhan. Falling from the heavens as a star-wound, it impacted Vvardenfell and formed Red Mountain. In Tower metaphysics, this First Stone anchors Red Tower and enables Mundus to persist without full divine presence, granting Nirn its variable fate. The Dwemer discovered the Heart and forged tools to harness its power for a brass god, but vanished instead. Later, the Tribunal and Dagoth Ur drew upon it to achieve divinity, visiting annually to renew their power until Dagoth Ur severed their access. Some traditions hold that the Heart creates Heroes to defend the mortal plane, and that the red gem of the Amulet of Kings originated as a drop of its blood.
topic_desc_basic: The Heart of Lorkhan is the divine spark of the dead god Lorkhan. Legend holds that it fell from the sky as a meteor, forming Red Mountain in Vvardenfell. The Dwemer discovered it and attempted to harness its power, but mysteriously vanished. Later, the Tribunal and Dagoth Ur used the Heart to become living gods.

title: Propylon Chambers
topic_desc: The Propylon Chambers are ancient teleportation devices housed within the ten Dunmer strongholds of Vvardenfell. Each chamber connects to neighboring strongholds through a network of magical pathways, enabling instantaneous transit across considerable distances. The system requires a Propylon Index—a specialized focusing crystal keyed to a specific destination—to activate transit to that stronghold. Without the appropriate index, the propylon remains inert. The indices are rare and scattered, their locations often unknown or guarded. The network stands as a testament to Dunmer architectural and arcane achievement, though much of its operational knowledge has been lost over the centuries, leaving the chambers largely dormant and their full potential unrealized.
topic_desc_basic: Ancient teleportation chambers built within the Dunmer strongholds of Vvardenfell. The propylon network permits instantaneous travel between strongholds, though each destination requires its corresponding Propylon Index to activate. Most chambers now lie dormant, their indices lost or scattered.

title: The Dunmer
topic_desc: The Dunmer, commonly called Dark Elves in the Empire, are the grey-skinned, red-eyed elven peoples of Morrowind. Embracing their reputation as ill-favored by fate, they are generally grim and aloof, combining powerful intellects with strong physiques to produce renowned warriors and sorcerers. Their culture revolves around the veneration of ancestors; spirits are bound by duty to aid their living bloodlines through family shrines and ghost fences. While foreign cultures mistakenly conflate these practices with necromancy—an abhorrent abomination to the Dunmer when performed upon elven remains—spirits of other races are afforded no such protection. The Great Ghost Fence, built by the Tribunal, has largely supplanted traditional clan fences, absorbing the remains of countless heroes to hold back the Blight.
topic_desc_basic: The Dunmer, or Dark Elves, are the grey-skinned, red-eyed elven natives of Morrowind. Fierce and reserved, they are renowned warriors and sorcerers who integrate the sword, bow, and destruction magic in battle. Their society centers on ancestor veneration, maintaining family shrines and ghost fences to commune with the dead—a practice outsiders often mistakenly condemn as necromancy.

title: Morrowind
topic_desc: Morrowind, historically known as Dwemereth, Veloth, and Resdayn, is the northeastern nation of Tamriel and the homeland of the Dunmer. Dominated by the volcanic Red Mountain and the island of Vvardenfell, it also encompasses mainland territory separated by the Inner Sea and bordered by the Sea of Ghosts. The province is governed under the Tribunal Temple's theocracy, with Great Houses holding secular power. Its landscape ranges from the ash-blighted interior to varied coastal and border regions. The island of Solstheim to the northwest remains a theoretical claim. Presently, Morrowind contends with the Blight spreading from Red Mountain and the rising threat of the Sixth House.
topic_desc_basic: Morrowind is the northeastern province of Tamriel and the homeland of the Dunmer. It consists of the mainland and the great island of Vvardenfell, which is dominated by the ash-spewing Red Mountain. Separated by the Inner Sea and bordered by the Sea of Ghosts, the region is also known historically as Resdayn or Veloth.

title: The Tribunal
topic_desc: The Tribunal—Almalexia, Sotha Sil, and Vivec, collectively Almsivi—are the Living Gods of the Dunmer and the central figures of the native Tribunal Temple faith. For millennia, they have guided and protected Morrowind, their divine authority and sustained power forming the bedrock of Dunmer religious and cultural identity. The Temple itself wields immense authority, controlling sacred sites like Ghostgate and the city of Vivec while maintaining strong ties with the pious Great Houses, particularly Indoril and Redoran. Though the faith accepts outlanders, few join sincerely. Tensions persist with Imperial institutions, as the Temple remains proscribed to adherents of the Imperial cult. The Tribunal's presence defines Morrowind's spiritual landscape.
topic_desc_basic: The Tribunal, or Almsivi, are the three Living Gods of the Dunmer: Almalexia, Sotha Sil, and Vivec. They are the central figures of the Tribunal Temple, the native religion of Morrowind, which wields great authority over the province's spiritual and cultural life.

title: Balmora
topic_desc: Balmora, meaning Stonewood in the Dunmeri tongue, is the district seat of House Hlaalu and Vvardenfell's second largest settlement after Vivec. Situated at the southern edge of the West Gash, it commands a strategic crossroads where the Ashlands, Bitter Coast marshes, and Ascadian Isles plantations converge. The Odai River divides the city into four districts: High Town on the eastern bluffs, the Commercial District, Labor Town to the west, and the Imperial Moonmoth Legion Fort just north. Though originally a Redoran stronghold, Hlaalu acquired the city through shrewd business and architectural maneuvering, transforming it into a prosperous mercantile hub reflecting their cosmopolitan values.
topic_desc_basic: Balmora is the district seat of House Hlaalu and Vvardenfell's second largest settlement. Located in the West Gash along the Odai River, it serves as a major mercantile hub. The city is divided into High Town, the Commercial District, Labor Town, and Moonmoth Legion Fort.

title: Vvardenfell
topic_desc: Vvardenfell, also called the Black Isle, is a large island within Morrowind's Inner Sea, dominated by the great volcano Red Mountain. Named after the Dwemeri term for that peak, meaning City of the Strong Shield, its landscape of arid wastes, rocky highlands, and coastal wetlands undergoes constant renewal from eruptions and ash-fall. Originally home to House Dagoth and a Dwemer kingdom, the entire territory became a Tribunal Temple preserve following the Battle of Red Mountain. Under the Armistice, the Temple restricted settlement and trade. In 3E 414, Vvardenfell was reorganized into an Imperial Provincial District divided into Redoran, Hlaalu, Telvanni, and Temple districts, each administered locally but overseen by Duke Dren and the District Council in Ebonheart. By 3E 427, heavy colonization has reduced native Dunmer to roughly half the population, while Dagoth Ur's spreading Ash Blight increasingly afflicts the island's environment and inhabitants.
topic_desc_basic: Vvardenfell is a large island within Morrowind's Inner Sea, dominated by the great volcano Red Mountain. Its landscape of arid wastes, rocky highlands, and coastal wetlands is constantly reshaped by eruptions and ash-fall. Formerly a Tribunal Temple preserve with restricted access, the island was reorganized as an Imperial Provincial District in 3E 414, opening it to increased Great House and outlander colonization.

title: The Nerevarine
topic_desc: The prophesied reincarnation of the Chimeri warlord Indoril Nerevar, whose return is foretold to defeat Dagoth Ur and restore Resdayn. The Nerevarine Cult holds that Nerevar cursed the ring Moon-and-Star so that none but his reincarnate could wear it. The Incarnate must survive corprus, don Moon-and-Star, and be named Hortator and Nerevarine by the Great Houses and Ashlander tribes. Whether the figure is a true soul-rebirth or a destiny-fulfilling individual remains contested between the Dissident Priests and orthodox Temple doctrine.
topic_desc_basic: A prophesied hero of Ashlander belief, held to be the reincarnation of Indoril Nerevar. The Nerevarine is destined to cast down the false gods, end the Blight, and restore Resdayn. The Temple denounces this doctrine as heresy.

title: The Nerevarine Prophecies
topic_desc: The Nerevarine Prophecies are Ashlander traditions foretelling the reincarnation of Indoril Nerevar. Centered on the Seven Visions and Seven Trials, they predict the Incarnate will unite the Dunmer, cast down the false Tribunal, and drive the Blight from Resdayn. The Tribunal Temple fiercely suppresses these teachings as heresy, though the predicted signs—including the moon-and-star ring and the outsider's arrival—remain central to millennial anticipation.
topic_desc_basic: Ashlander traditions hold that Indoril Nerevar will be reincarnated to save the Dunmer. The prophecies describe seven trials the Incarnate must overcome to cast down false gods and end the Blight. The Tribunal Temple condemns these teachings as heresy.

title: The Sixth House
topic_desc: The Sixth House, originally House Dagoth, was the sixth Great House of the Chimer. Following the Battle of Red Mountain, its records were destroyed and its surviving members were absorbed into the remaining houses, earning it the epithet 'the Tribe Unmourned.' Unbeknownst to the world, Dagoth Ur survived within Red Mountain, gradually building power and influence. Operating from citadels like Kogoruhn, he commands ash vampires and corrupted dreamers, seeking to overthrow the Tribunal and reshape Morrowind through the power of the Heart of Lorkhan and a new Numidium.
topic_desc_basic: The Sixth House, originally House Dagoth, was the defunct sixth Great House of the Chimer. After the Battle of Red Mountain, its records were destroyed and its surviving members were absorbed into other houses. Unbeknownst to the outside world, Dagoth Ur survived within Red Mountain and spent centuries building power, seeking to overthrow the Tribunal and conquer Morrowind.
aliases: Sixth House and the Tribe Unmourned

title: Red Mountain
topic_desc: Red Mountain is a massive volcano dominating the island of Vvardenfell in Morrowind. Originally the highest peak in Tamriel, its summit is visible from Mournhold on clear days. The island takes its name from the Dwemeris designation for the mountain, meaning City of the Strong Shield. Red Mountain has erupted catastrophically multiple times, including the Sun's Death event and the Days of Fire. The Tribunal encircled the mountain with the Ghostfence to contain the Ash Blight, restricting physical access primarily to Ghostgate. Within this perimeter lie deep lava ravines called foyada, blighted creatures, and four ancient Dwemer citadels serving as strongholds for Dagoth Ur and his ash vampires. The mountain holds profound mythological significance as the Red Tower, with the Heart of Lorkhan serving as its Stone, anchoring Mundus with variable fate. The Battle of Red Mountain occurred on its slopes, resulting in the Dwemer disappearance and the Tribunal's ascension.
topic_desc_basic: Red Mountain is a vast volcano dominating the island of Vvardenfell. Visible from Mournhold, it is considered the most dangerous region in Morrowind. The Tribunal built the Ghostfence around it to contain the Ash Blight, with Ghostgate serving as the primary entrance. Ash storms and blighted creatures plague the interior, where ancient Dwemer citadels serve as strongholds for Dagoth Ur and his minions.

title: The Chimer
topic_desc: The Chimer, meaning People of the North, are the Aldmeri dissidents who followed the prophet Veloth from Summerset Isle to settle Morrowind. Rejecting Aedric worship, they embraced the Good Daedra—Boethiah, Azura, and Mephala—whose teachings shaped their dynamic, ambitious culture of fundamentalist ancestor worship. Resembling the Altmer but with paler golden skin, they established the High Velothi culture and raised great temples to their Daedric patrons. Their civilization ended at the Battle of Red Mountain, when Azura's curse transformed them into the Dunmer. A few figures, notably Almalexia and partially Vivec, retained their Chimeri appearance despite this curse.
topic_desc_basic: The Chimer were Aldmeri clans who followed the prophet Veloth from Summerset to Morrowind, worshipping the Daedra Boethiah, Azura, and Mephala. They built a golden-skinned civilization devoted to ancestor worship before being cursed and transformed into the Dunmer after the Battle of Red Mountain.

title: The Dwemer
topic_desc: The Dwemer, commonly called Dwarves or Deep Elves, are a fabled lost race of Mer that vanished in 1E 700. Devoted to reason, science, and the arcane over faith, they built elaborate underground cities and crafted enigmatic mechanical constructs. Their agnostic culture often clashed with the Daedra-worshipping Chimer, though the two united under the First Council to repel Nordic invaders before warring over the profane Heart of Lorkhan. The Rourken clan exiled itself westward to Hammerfell, while other clans established holdings in Skyrim. The entire race mysteriously disappeared during the War of the First Council, leaving behind only their enigmatic ruins, mechanical guardians, and enduring mysteries.
topic_desc_basic: The Dwemer, or Deep Elves, were a reclusive race of Mer known as Dwarves who mysteriously vanished in 1E 700. They were highly skilled engineers and enchanters who built vast underground cities and mechanical guardians across Morrowind, Hammerfell, and Skyrim. Their agnostic society preferred reason over religion, frequently clashing with their Daedra-worshipping Chimer neighbors. Their sudden disappearance left their ruins and artifacts scattered across Tamriel.

title: The Ghostfence
topic_desc: The Great Ghost Fence is an enormous wall encircling the crater of Red Mountain, raised by the Tribunal to contain the Blight and corprus monsters within the Red Mountain region. Its pillars channel the holy energies of Almsivi and the spirits of the deceased, forming an impenetrable shield. Constructed in standard Temple architectural style, it has stood since shortly after the Armistice in the late Second Era and is centuries old. The only conventional entrance lies at the gate citadel of Ghostgate, though a tunnel through Kogoruhn also breaches the barrier. Levitation and cliff racers can pass over the wall. The period around 3E 417 is sometimes called the time of the Ghostfence. Pilgrims following the Seven Graces must pass through the fence to reach the Shrine of Pride.
topic_desc_basic: The Great Ghost Fence is a vast wall surrounding Red Mountain, sustained by the Tribunal's combined powers to keep the Blight and corprus monsters contained. The only conventional entrance is at Ghostgate. It has stood for centuries since shortly after the Armistice.

title: Corprus
topic_desc: Corprus, meaning 'skin blight' in Ald Chimeris, encompasses various skin ailments afflicting the Dunmer. Ranging from mild blemishes to lethal plagues, these maladies stem from natural causes like poor hygiene and parasites, or unnatural alchemical and magical origins. However, the term is most notoriously applied to the Divine Disease, a horrific supernatural blight created by Dagoth Ur. This corprus twists victims into grotesque, agonized mutants, eroding their minds while unnaturally bolstering their physical resilience, ultimately reducing them to shambling corprus beasts or mindless servants of the Sixth House.
topic_desc_basic: Corprus, meaning 'skin blight' in Ald Chimeris, refers to various skin ailments common among the Dunmer. These range from natural blemishes caused by poor hygiene to severe magical plagues. Most notoriously, the term describes the Divine Disease, a horrific supernatural blight created by Dagoth Ur that twists victims into grotesque, mindless mutants.

title: Vivec
topic_desc: Vivec, known as the Warrior-Poet, is the Guardian God-King of Vvardenfell and a member of the Tribunal alongside Almalexia and Sotha Sil. He embodies the spirit and duality of the Dunmer people, reflected in his half-Chimer, half-Dunmer aspect. Before apotheosis, he served as Hortator Indoril Nerevar's general, though accounts of his mortal origins range from a netchiman's son to a divine egg-image associated with the Daedric Prince Mephala. A prolific writer, his cryptic 36 Lessons serve as a guide for the prophesied Nerevarine. He resides in his palace at the summit of Vivec City, the holy canton capital of Vvardenfell, guarding the land from the dark gods of Red Mountain. His legendary spear is Muatra.
topic_desc_basic: Lord Vivec, the Warrior-Poet, is one of the three Living Gods of the Tribunal and the Guardian God-King of Vvardenfell. He embodies Dunmer duality and is renowned for both martial prowess and cryptic poetry. He resides within his palace in Vivec City, ever vigilant against the forces of Red Mountain.

title: Sotha Sil
topic_desc: Sotha Sil, or Seht, is the wizard-mystic god of the Dunmer and the most reclusive member of the Tribunal. Known as the Mainspring Ever-Wound and the Clockwork God, he is the patron of artificers and wizards. He brokered the Coldharbour Compact with eight Daedric Princes to restrict their direct interference in mortal affairs. He dwells within his Clockwork City, a mechanical realm served by fabricants and Clockwork Apostles devoted to achieving Tamriel Final. To free himself from the burden of emotion, he extracted his memories into the Mnemonic Planisphere. He does not believe in free will or his own divinity, viewing himself as bound to his creations and burdened by absolute certainty, coveting the word 'maybe' above all others.
topic_desc_basic: Sotha Sil, called Seht, is the reclusive wizard-mystic god of the Dunmer and a member of the Tribunal. Known as the Clockwork God and patron of artificers, he negotiated the Coldharbour Compact limiting Daedric interference in mortal affairs. He resides within his Clockwork City, endlessly creating mechanical wonders, and rarely appears among his followers.

title: Dagoth Ur
topic_desc: Once Voryn Dagoth, Lord High Councilor of House Dagoth and companion of Hortator Indoril Nerevar, he reported the Dwemer's profane discovery of the Heart of Lorkhan, inadvertently sparking the Battle of Red Mountain. Accounts of his actions during the conflict fiercely diverge, but the aftermath saw his house condemned as traitors and his name demonized by the Tribunal Temple as the Sharmat and the Devil. Surviving his apparent death, he slept beneath Red Mountain for millennia. Upon reawakening, he stole divine power from the Tribunal, spread the Blight and corprus across Morrowind, and sought to build Akulakhan to conquer Tamriel.
topic_desc_basic: Known to the Tribunal Temple as the Sharmat and the Devil, Dagoth Ur is the immortal enemy of the Dunmer people. Once the lord of the extinct House Dagoth, he slept beneath Red Mountain for ages before reawakening. He spreads the Blight and corprus disease from his stronghold, seeking to conquer all of Morrowind.

title: Indoril Nerevar
topic_desc: Indoril Nerevar, the Chimer Hortator and King of Resdayn, forged the First Council with the Dwemer in 1E 416. He died following the Battle of Red Mountain circa 1E 700 under fiercely disputed circumstances. The Tribunal Temple venerates him as Saint Nerevar, patron of warriors and House Redoran, while Ashlander cults await his prophesied return as the Nerevarine to cast down false gods and restore the ancestral promises.
topic_desc_basic: Indoril Nerevar is the ancient Chimer king and Hortator who united his people against the Dwemer at the Battle of Red Mountain. He died under disputed circumstances shortly after this victory. The Tribunal Temple honors him as Saint Nerevar, while Ashlanders revere him as a prophet and await his reincarnation as the Nerevarine.

title: Azura
topic_desc: Azura, called the Queen of Dawn and Dusk, is a Daedric Prince whose sphere encompasses the liminal transitions of twilight, alongside mystery, magic, fate, and prophecy. She maintains a distinctly female image and commands an exceptionally devoted following, as she desires the love of her mortal subjects above all else. To the Dunmer, she is revered as one of the good Daedra and recognized as the Anticipation of Sotha Sil. The Ashlander tribes particularly uphold her ancient veneration, acknowledging her as cruel but wise. The Khajiit know her as Azurah, crediting her with introducing moon sugar to their kind. Her Oblivion realm is Moonshadow, and her summoning day is Hogithum, the 21st of First Seed.
topic_desc_basic: Azura is a Daedric Prince of dawn and dusk, mystery, and prophecy. Known as the Queen of Dawn and Dusk, she is one of the few Daedra perceived as benevolent toward mortals, demanding their love and devotion. The Dunmer revere her as one of the good Daedra and the Anticipation of Sotha Sil, with the Ashlander tribes maintaining particularly strong veneration of her ancient traditions.

title: Barenziah
topic_desc: Barenziah is one of the most famous figures of the Third Era, serving as the first Queen of Morrowind under Imperial vassalage alongside her consort, the general Symmachus. Popular with the Dunmer yet largely ceremonial, she supported the Empire against Uriel Septim III during the War of the Red Diamond. Following Symmachus's death in a riot circa 3E 391, she abdicated and went into exile. She later played a crucial role in toppling the impostor Jagar Tharn and ending the Imperial Simulacrum, subsequently marrying King Eadwyre of Wayrest. Following the Miracle of Peace and Eadwyre's death, she returned to Morrowind as Queen Mother when her son Helseth claimed the throne. Her life remains subject to rumor and disputed biographical accounts.
topic_desc_basic: Barenziah was the first Queen of Morrowind under Imperial vassalage. After her consort Symmachus was killed and she was forced to abdicate, she went into exile. She later helped overthrow the impostor Jagar Tharn, ending the Imperial Simulacrum, and subsequently married King Eadwyre of Wayrest. She eventually returned to Morrowind to serve as Queen Mother when her son Helseth became King.

title: Divayth Fyr
topic_desc: Divayth Fyr is an ancient Dunmer sorcerer of Great House Telvanni, estimated at four thousand years old. Though he holds no seat on the Telvanni Council, he serves as an advisor and upholds their directives. A former Psijic Order member, he is compared to mages like Shalidor and Vanus Galerion. He resides in Tel Fyr on Vvardenfell, where he maintains the Corprusarium—a sanctuary for corprus victims, including the last living Dwarf, Yagrum Bagarn. He lives alongside four female clones he calls his daughters.
topic_desc_basic: Divayth Fyr is a four-thousand-year-old Dunmer sorcerer of Great House Telvanni. He resides in his tower of Tel Fyr on Vvardenfell, where he maintains the Corprusarium, a sanctuary for those afflicted with corprus disease. There, he cares for Yagrum Bagarn, the last living Dwarf. Fyr lives alongside four female clones of himself whom he calls his daughters.

title: Yagrum Bagarn
topic_desc: Yagrum Bagarn is the last known living Dwemer, surviving the mysterious disappearance of his people. Formerly a Master Crafter in service to Lord Kagrenac, the chief Tonal Architect, he was absent during the calamity at Red Mountain. Upon returning to find his race vanished, he searched extensively for answers but contracted Corprus disease. Bloated and afflicted, he resides in the Corprusarium beneath Tel Fyr under the care of Divayth Fyr, who restored his sanity but failed to cure his body. A learned scholar, Yagrum studies theories of the disappearance and provides insight into Kagrenac's tools and texts such as Divine Metaphysics and The Egg of Time.
topic_desc_basic: Yagrum Bagarn is the last known living Dwemer. Bloated and afflicted with Corprus disease, he resides in the Corprusarium beneath Tel Fyr, cared for by the ancient wizard Divayth Fyr. He is a rare living source of knowledge on the Dwemer and their mysterious disappearance.

title: Caius Cosades
topic_desc: Caius Cosades is the Imperial Grand Spymaster of the Blades operating in Vvardenfell. Stationed in Balmora, he poses as a skooma-addicted layabout, though his tolerance and sharp instincts betray his true nature. As the ranking Blades agent in the district, he directs intelligence efforts concerning the Sixth House and the Nerevarine prophecies. His superiors eventually recall him to the Imperial City amid concerns regarding his genuine addiction to moon sugar.
topic_desc_basic: Caius Cosades is the Imperial Grand Spymaster of the Blades in Vvardenfell. Operating from Balmora, he maintains a cover as a skooma-addicted old man while directing the Empire's intelligence network regarding the Sixth House threat.

title: The Tribunal Temple
topic_desc: The Tribunal Temple is the native religion of the Dunmer, venerating the living gods Almalexia, Sotha Sil, and Vivec—collectively Almsivi. Under the Armistice, Vvardenfell remains a Temple preserve encompassing the city of Vivec, Ghostgate, and all sacred sites within the Ghostfence. The Temple holds strong bonds with the pious Houses Indoril and Redoran, and maintains amicable ties with Dres and Hlaalu. Relations with Imperial guilds are strained; the Temple sits on the Empire's Proscribed List of Hostile Cults, forbidding courtesy membership to adherents of the Imperial Citizenship Cult. While outlanders may join, most do so for services rather than faith. The Temple guards orthodoxy fiercely, suppressing dissenting cults and protecting Morrowind from the Blight emanating from Red Mountain.
topic_desc_basic: The Tribunal Temple is the native religion of the Dunmer, worshipping the living gods Almalexia, Sotha Sil, and Vivec, known as Almsivi. It controls the Vvardenfell district as a Temple preserve under the Armistice. The Temple maintains strong ties with Houses Indoril and Redoran, but strained relations with Imperial organizations.

title: The Morag Tong
topic_desc: The Morag Tong is an ancient guild of assassins headquartered in Morrowind, operating in the name of Mephala. Active since at least the First Era, the Tong holds a unique sanctioned status under the Morrowind government, legally performing executions bound by contracts known as writs. Extralegal gray writs are also rumored to exist. The Great Houses frequently employ the Tong to eliminate rivals, providing a preferred alternative to open warfare. The Tong's doctrine holds that Mephala grows stronger with every murder in her name, but certain killings please her more; murders born of hate surpass those driven by greed, and the slaying of great figures outweighs the deaths of unknowns. This philosophy originates from the guild's first leader, the original Night Mother.
topic_desc_basic: The Morag Tong is an ancient guild of assassins operating in Morrowind in the name of Mephala. Uniquely sanctioned by the Morrowind government, the guild performs legal executions under contracts called writs, though extralegal gray writs are rumored. The Great Houses frequently employ the Tong to settle disputes and eliminate rivals without open conflict.

title: Great House Hlaalu
topic_desc: Great House Hlaalu is one of the five traditional Great Houses of the settled Dunmer, governing the Hlaalu District of western-central Morrowind from its ancient capital of Narsis. On Vvardenfell, its council seat resides in Balmora, with additional holdings in Suran, Hla Oad, and Gnaar Mok. Distinguished by its adaptability and opportunism, the house prioritizes business and diplomacy, valuing a good reputation alongside profit. Its willingness to embrace foreign cultures and Imperial trade sets it apart from more xenophobic Dunmer houses. This Imperial favor brings political and economic dominance, yet also invites corruption; many Hlaalu leaders and retainers are notoriously bribable, employing theft, blackmail, and espionage as readily as honest commerce. The house maintains positive ties with the Empire, the Tribunal Temple, and the Camonna Tong, while facing animosity from Houses Redoran, Telvanni, and Indoril. Its heraldry is the Golden Scales, and its patron saint is Veloth the Pilgrim.
topic_desc_basic: Great House Hlaalu is an adaptable and opportunistic Dunmer Great House that dominates trade and maintains close ties with the Empire. Governed from its Balmora council seat on Vvardenfell, the house values profit, diplomacy, and foreign tolerance, setting it apart from more xenophobic Dunmer factions. Its retainers are skilled merchants and spies, though notoriously bribable.

title: Great House Redoran
topic_desc: Great House Redoran is one of the five remaining Great Houses of the Dunmer, governing the northwestern Redoran District from Blacklight. Steeped in tradition and piety, it champions the way of the warrior, long serving as Morrowind's de facto military. The Tribunal Temple is its natural ally, supplying many Buoyant Armigers, while Saint Nerevar the Captain serves as its patron. Redoran respects martial strength, holding the Fighters Guild and Imperial Legion in higher esteem than other Imperial institutions. It maintains strained relations with House Hlaalu, House Telvanni, the Morag Tong, and Ashlander tribes, but respects House Indoril and will fight alongside House Dres. On Vvardenfell, its council convenes in Ald'ruhn-under-Skar, within a colossal emperor crab shell.
topic_desc_basic: Great House Redoran is one of the five Great Houses of the Dunmer. Focused on martial skill and ancient tradition, it often serves as the military backbone of the Dunmer people and the Tribunal Temple. Distrustful of most Imperial institutions, Redoran respects only martial strength. Its Vvardenfell council seat is in Ald'ruhn-under-Skar.

title: Great House Telvanni
topic_desc: Great House Telvanni is one of the Great Houses of Morrowind, governing the Telvanni District of the northeast and the eastern reaches of Vvardenfell from its council seat in Sadrith Mora. Comprised primarily of reclusive, egocentric wizard-lords, the House prizes arcane mastery, knowledge, and the forceful expression of individual will. Its members traditionally isolate themselves within towering fungal strongholds, pursuing solitary research and shunning outside politics. A minority of ambitious mages compete ruthlessly for Vvardenfell's resources, though the House publicly denies supporting these rogue factions. Advancement within Telvanni is notoriously ruthless; members often rise by eliminating or indisposing rivals. The Telvanni fiercely reject external authority, particularly that of the Mages Guild, and maintain a notorious tolerance of vampires. They are careless in observance of Tribunal doctrine, favoring ancestor worship instead.
topic_desc_basic: Great House Telvanni is a Great House of Morrowind dominated by reclusive wizard-lords. Governing the northeast and eastern Vvardenfell from Sadrith Mora, its members pursue arcane mastery within towering fungal strongholds. Telvanni society is ruthless and isolationist; mages advance by eliminating rivals, reject outside authority like the Mages Guild, and uniquely tolerate vampires.

title: Slavery in Morrowind
topic_desc: Slavery is a legally protected institution in Morrowind, sustained by the Armistice of 2E 896, which exempted the province from the Empire's general abolition. The Dunmer consider slave ownership an ancient right, primarily raiding Black Marsh and Elsweyr for Argonian and Khajiit captives. Enslaved individuals are restrained by magical bracers and held in plantations, mines, and Telvanni markets. Abolitionist movements, notably the Twin Lamps, actively oppose the practice, aiding escapees and operating through safe havens like the Argonian Mission in Ebonheart. The tension between Imperial law and Dunmer tradition makes slavery a deeply divisive issue across Vvardenfell.
topic_desc_basic: Slavery is legally protected in Morrowind under the Armistice, though it is outlawed elsewhere in the Empire. The Dunmer primarily enslave Argonians and Khajiit, holding them in plantations and mines using magical bracers. Abolitionist groups like the Twin Lamps resist this practice and help escaped slaves find refuge.

title: Seyda Neen
topic_desc: Seyda Neen is a House Hlaalu port village in the southern Bitter Coast, bordering the Ascadian Isles. Known as the Gateway to Vvardenfell, it serves as a vital waypoint for Imperial travelers entering or leaving the island. The Empire maintains a Coastguard station and Census and Excise Office at the harbor, processing arrivals and restocking Imperial cutters that patrol against smugglers. The Grand Pharos, a renowned lighthouse at the harbor mouth, guides mariners throughout the Inner Sea. Over the centuries, the village has absorbed Imperial, Nordic, and Dunmeri architectural elements. Silt striders offer overland transport to Balmora, Gnisis, Suran, and Vivec.
topic_desc_basic: Seyda Neen is a small House Hlaalu port village in the southern Bitter Coast, widely known as the Gateway to Vvardenfell. Imperial travelers are processed through its Census and Excise Office, and the Grand Pharos lighthouse guides mariners navigating the Inner Sea. Silt striders provide transport to major destinations across the island.

title: Vivec City
topic_desc: Vivec City, the largest settlement on Vvardenfell, serves as the holy seat of the Tribunal Temple on the island. Named for the Warrior-Poet Vivec, who resides within its boundaries, the city is also called the City of Swords for the laws that cut citizens into better shape. Constructed across nine artificial cantons in Norvayn Bay on Vvardenfell's southern coast, each island-canton is a massive multi-tiered structure the size of a small town, connected by bridges and walkways over seawater canals. The cantons are organized into Underworks, Canalworks, Waistworks, and Plaza tiers. Ordinators, the Temple's militant order, police the city, though they avoid the Underworks. The Ministry of Truth, a celestial body suspended above the city by Vivec, looms as both a monument and a threat.
topic_desc_basic: Vivec City is the largest city in Vvardenfell, situated on the southern coast. Named after the god Vivec, it is the holy seat of the Tribunal Temple on the island. The city consists of nine artificial cantons—massive multi-tiered buildings connected by bridges and walkways over water. Ordinators of the Temple serve as its guards. The Ministry of Truth floats above the city.

title: Mournhold
topic_desc: Mournhold, also called Mourning Hold, the City of Light and Magic, the City of Gems, and the City of Love and Charity, is a major mainland Morrowind city in the Deshaan region. As the district seat of Great House Indoril and the epicenter of the Tribunal Temple, it draws pilgrims and priests to Mournhold Temple, the palace of the god-king Almalexia. Both the city and its surrounding metropolis share her name. Built atop the underground ruins of Old Mournhold, it is perhaps the largest and oldest settlement in the province, renowned for its grand, majestic architecture despite a brooding reputation. It has long served as the capital of Morrowind.
topic_desc_basic: Mournhold is a major city in mainland Morrowind's Deshaan region. Known as the City of Light and Magic, it is the district seat of House Indoril and the epicenter of the Tribunal Temple. Pilgrims travel to Mournhold Temple, the palace of the god-king Almalexia. The city and its surrounding metropolis are also called Almalexia.

title: Solstheim
topic_desc: Solstheim, meaning Sun's Home, is a large island in the Sea of Ghosts north of Tamriel. The Snow Elves were its first inhabitants, building grand settlements that outlasted their mainland holdings. Nordic influence has traditionally dominated the island, which is home to the Skaal, a reclusive tribe maintaining ancient traditions. Southern Solstheim suffers from continuous ash deposits blown from Red Mountain on Vvardenfell, devastating once-fertile pine forests and settlements, while the northern reaches retain their harsh, frozen character.
topic_desc_basic: Solstheim is a large, frigid island in the Sea of Ghosts north of Tamriel. Snow Elves were its first inhabitants, though Nordic influence has traditionally dominated. The Skaal tribe resides here, and ash from Red Mountain continually afflicts the island's southern half.

title: The Skaal
topic_desc: The Skaal are an isolated tribe of Nords inhabiting a village along Solstheim's Felsaad Coast, near Lake Fjalding. According to their oral traditions, they descend from Dragon Cult loyalists who survived a cataclysmic battle that severed Solstheim from the Skyrim mainland. This heritage and profound isolation fostered a distinct culture centered on the worship of the All-Maker. Unlike mainstream Nords, the Skaal strive to live in harmony with nature, relying entirely on the land for their needs and rarely accepting coin from travelers. Their settlement, the northernmost in Tamriel, consists of sturdy wooden homes arranged around a central Greathall. While they can be hospitable, Skaal Honor Guards clad in traditional Nordic mail vigilantly protect the village from intruders.
topic_desc_basic: The Skaal are an isolated tribe of Nords dwelling in a village on Solstheim's Felsaad Coast. They diverge from mainstream Nordic culture by striving to live in harmony with nature, guided by their worship of the All-Maker. Their settlement, the northernmost in Tamriel, is defended by vigilant Honor Guards.

title: Scribs
topic_desc: Scribs are the larval stage of the kwama, large insects native to Morrowind whose colonies form the basis of the Dunmer egg mining economy. Though not aggressive, scribs defend themselves by secreting a substance that induces paralysis. Scrib jelly is harvested as a common food and alchemical ingredient. The scrib's image appears on banners throughout Vvardenfell to denote nearby taverns, reflecting its deep cultural familiarity among the Dunmer.
topic_desc_basic: Scribs are the larval form of the kwama, large insects kept in colonies for their eggs. Though unaggressive, they can paralyze attackers. Scrib jelly is a common Dunmer food, and the scrib image marks tavern banners across Vvardenfell.

title: Silt Striders
topic_desc: Silt Striders are giant arthropods native to Morrowind, towering up to sixty feet high. Their tough carapaces allow them to endure Vvardenfell's harsh environments and survive the Ash Blight that exterminated many native species. Domesticated by the Dunmer, they serve as the primary civilian transport across an elaborate network connecting the island's cities. Caravaners steer the creatures by directly manipulating exposed organs and tissues using specialized hooks. Since the arthropods lack natural cavities, passenger and cargo compartments are hollowed directly into their chitinous shells. Cities like Gnisis and Molag Mar maintain dedicated docks to facilitate trade shipments. Desiccated remains frequently dot the Ashlands, testament to the creatures' enduring presence in the region.
topic_desc_basic: Silt Striders are towering giant arthropods native to Morrowind, commonly used as the primary means of civilian transport across Vvardenfell. Dunmer caravaners steer them by manipulating exposed organs with specialized hooks. Passengers and cargo ride in compartments hollowed directly into the creatures' chitinous shells.

title: Kagrenac's Tools
topic_desc: Kagrenac's Tools are three legendary Dwemer artifacts—Wraithguard, Keening, and Sunder—forged by Lord Kagrenac to tap the divine power of Lorkhan's Heart. Wraithguard is a protective gauntlet, Sunder a hammer to strike the heart and draw power, and Keening a blade to flay and focus that power. Kagrenac's use of these tools during the Battle of Red Mountain coincided with the complete disappearance of the Dwemer. Recovered by Lord Nerevar and Voryn Dagoth, the tools became the center of a fatal dispute. The Tribunal later broke their oath and used them to attain godhood, while Dagoth Ur's unguarded exposure fused him to the Heart. The Dissident Priests consider these artifacts cursed, arguing that their corrupting influence has doomed both the Tribunal and Dagoth Ur.
topic_desc_basic: Kagrenac's Tools are three Dwemer artifacts—Wraithguard, Keening, and Sunder—created to draw upon the divine power of Lorkhan's Heart. Their use at the Battle of Red Mountain coincided with the disappearance of the Dwemer. The Tribunal later used them to attain godhood, though many consider the tools cursed and inherently corrupting.

title: Keening
topic_desc: Keening is a legendary Dwemer short blade forged by Lord Kagrenac, Tonal Architect of the lost Dwemer race. Alongside Sunder and Wraithguard, it forms the essential toolset required to tap the mythic power of the Heart of Lorkhan. Following the Battle of Red Mountain, the Tribunal claimed the tools, though Keening and Sunder were eventually lost during a Third Era pilgrimage to the Heart. The blade now rests within the Odrosal citadel, deep within the Red Mountain region. Keening channels profound tonal resonances; to wield it barehanded is to suffer immediate mortal devastation, necessitating Wraithguard's protective enchantment to safely harness its power.
topic_desc_basic: Keening is a legendary Dwemer dagger forged by Lord Kagrenac. Together with Sunder and Wraithguard, it is one of the three tools required to handle the Heart of Lorkhan. The Tribunal once possessed these artifacts after the Battle of Red Mountain, but Keening was later lost and remains hidden within the Red Mountain region.

title: Sunder
topic_desc: Sunder is a legendary Dwemer hammer crafted by Lord Kagrenac, Tonal Architect of the Dwemer. Alongside Keening and Wraithguard, it forms the toolset necessary to manipulate the Heart of Lorkhan. Following the Battle of Red Mountain, the Almsivi claimed all three tools, though Sunder and Keening were eventually lost during a Third Era pilgrimage to the Heart. The hammer currently resides within Vemynal, held by Dagoth Vemyn of the Sixth House. Without the protective ward of Wraithguard, handling Sunder inflicts a lethal mortal wound upon the wielder.
topic_desc_basic: Sunder is a legendary Dwemer hammer crafted by Lord Kagrenac to manipulate the Heart of Lorkhan. Alongside Keening and Wraithguard, it is essential for tapping the Heart's divine power. Following the Battle of Red Mountain, the Almsivi acquired the tools, but Sunder was later lost and fell into the hands of House Dagoth. It cannot be safely wielded without Wraithguard.

title: Wraithguard
topic_desc: Wraithguard is a legendary Dwemer gauntlet crafted by Lord Kagrenac, the Tonal Architect of the Dwemer. Designed to safely handle the profane tools Keening and Sunder, it is essential for any mortal seeking to tap the mythopoeic energies of the Heart of Lorkhan. Vivec holds the functioning right-hand version, offering it to the Nerevarine for the assault on Red Mountain. Should Vivec perish before bestowing it, the inactive artifact can be recovered and brought to the last living Dwarf, Yagrum Bagarn, who can harmonize it using Kagrenac's journal and planbook; however, activating this jury-rigged version without divine safeguards inflicts severe and permanent harm upon the wielder.
topic_desc_basic: Wraithguard is a legendary Dwemer gauntlet created by Lord Kagrenac. It allows mortals to safely handle Keening and Sunder, the tools required to manipulate the Heart of Lorkhan. Vivec possesses the functioning right-hand gauntlet and grants it to the Nerevarine.
